title: Mounting a rocket launcher atop Núi Bà Đen
description: Three men work over a large cylindrical launcher lashed to a wooden A-frame cradle inside a sandbagged position on the summit of Núi Bà Đen — two of them wearing green berets. Larry, who took the photograph, says they are setting up a rocket launcher taken off a Huey helicopter to fire down at a crossroad. He identifies Major Schwartzkoff (middle), an Australian captain (right), and — he thinks — a Captain Kennedy from Boston (left).

researchNotes: Account and identifications from Larry's Memories comments (2026-08-13; archived as data/recollections/giscus-vn-0006-c18006884.json and -c18006900.json). The two green berets visible corroborate the Special Forces presence Larry describes at the mountain camp (call sign Body Jab 42). Larry as photographer explains his absence from the frame. Research sweep 2026-08-13: no documented Vietnam-era instance of helicopter rocket pods dismounted for ground fire was found — the Army only formalized the idea in the mid-1970s ('the Slammer') — so if the identification holds, this photograph may be rare primary evidence of an otherwise unrecorded field improvisation.
